ledger.x: c. 3200 BCE: the ashmound Neolithic of the southern Deccan begins. 'these man-made accumulations of fossilised ash have been dated to the Neolithic period, approximately 3200 to 1200 BC'; 'Found primarily on the Deccan Plateau of southern India'. The year is the page's; the country is my reading of the named states…

c. 1200 BCE: the Neolithic ashmound tradition ends. 'approximately 3200 to 1200 BC'; 'while the ashmounds were initiated during the Neolithic, their use continued into the Iron Age' (upper layers at Palavoy show 'iron objects and Iron Age ceramics'). The Iron Age megalithic culture of the south has no dossier here.

certainty.note: A tradition known from over 200 ashmound sites; the page gives states, river valleys and districts, not frontiers.
